handoff.purpose: Fiedler vector sign pinning, cut edges, algebraic connectivity, boundary agreement, and modularity_report function.

symbols.name: modularity_report
symbols.note: Computes Newman modularity Q for declared partition and compares to random partitions with same block sizes.

claims.text: The sign of an eigenvector is arbitrary. Pin it so two runs over an unchanged tree produce the same dict -- provenance requires it.
claims.why: The code checks sum of values and sign of first ordered value, then multiplies by -1 if condition holds, pinning the sign.

claims.text: A disconnected graph's algebraic connectivity is exactly 0 -- that is the true global answer, and the component value is a DIFFERENT number about a DIFFERENT graph. Both are labelled so neither can be quoted as the other.
claims.why: Return dict has two keys: 'algebraic_connectivity_global' (0.0 if not connected else lambda2) and 'algebraic_connectivity_scope' (lambda2 always).

claims.text: declared is Newman modularity Q of the on-disk package partition.
claims.why: Code computes declared = float(nx.community.modularity(graph, blocks)) using blocks from _communities(partition, graph).

claims.text: random_mean is Q of partitions with the SAME block sizes and shuffled membership -- the null hypothesis, measured rather than assumed.
claims.why: Code shuffles nodes and creates random_blocks with same sizes, computes modularity, and averages samples.

claims.text: Q >= 0.3 with clear lift -- the package layout is real structure.
claims.why: The docstring gives interpretation advice, not a checkable claim in code. The code does not enforce or test this.
Interpretation advice, not a code claim.

claims.text: lift <= 0 -- the declared layout is NO BETTER than shuffling the files.
Q < 0 -- worse than random: blocks are internally sparser than chance.
Q is not comparable across different graphs -- only across snapshots of THIS graph.
If graph.number_of_edges() == 0, return _unavailable('a graph with no edges has undefined modularity').
claims.why: Code checks graph.number_of_edges() == 0 and returns _unavailable with that message.

claims.text: If len(blocks) < 2, return _unavailable('modularity needs at least 2 non-empty blocks').
claims.why: Code checks len(blocks) < 2 and returns _unavailable with that message.
The check is present (if not HAVE_MATH), but the constant MATH_EXTRA_HINT is not defined in this chunk.

observations.what: The variable 'partition' used in agreement calculation is not a parameter of the enclosing function; it must come from outer scope or closure.
The comment 'Stated verbatim so a reader never has to recall the scale.' refers to 'reads_as' values, which are indeed hardcoded strings.
The modularity_report function uses _communities and _unavailable which are not defined in this chunk.
The constant MATH_EXTRA_HINT is referenced but not defined in this chunk.
